claims.head: The Canadiens smell blood
claims.call: The Canadiens’ average shot has at least their usual 6.9% chance of going in.
claims.body: When the Canadiens shoot, it’s usually a real chance, and the Hurricanes are the league’s worst at stopping that. Brandon Bussi is going to be busy in all the wrong ways.
claims.nums: Montréal 1st for shot quality (a 6.9% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Carolina 32nd for preventing dangerous shots

claims.head: The Canadiens can’t afford to take penalties
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ power play creates at least their usual 8.3 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Canadiens’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Hurricanes’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canadiens tonight.

notes.text: Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 70% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 22 seconds at a time, against 63 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (10 of 13 changes).

MTL.head: A tough matchup for the Canadiens
MTL.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canadiens can pull it off if they get good looks.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes should have the upper hand
CAR.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canadiens can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: A rematch of last spring’s conference final
paras: The Hurricanes come in at 1-1-1, the Canadiens at 1-0-1. Two of the league’s best teams meet.
The Canadiens make their shots count, and the Hurricanes allow dangerous ones. Expect plenty of hitting.

items.text: First meeting since the Hurricanes beat the Canadiens in five games in last spring’s conference final, two of them in overtime.
The Hurricanes have been without Seth Jarvis all season.
The Canadiens are newly without Ivan Demidov.
Andrei Svechnikov has seven goals in nine games against Montréal since 2023-24.
